judge_reasoning: The line is rules-legal and wins this turn. Quarry Hauler raises Kiora to 8 loyalty; Kiora's emblem and Octopus triggers remove one Colossus and kill Festering Mummy; the Mummy places a -1/-1 counter on the second Colossus, triggering Hapatra to create a deathtouch Snake; the emblem lets that Snake fight and destroy the remaining Colossus. Hapatra and the untapped Weaver then attack for exactly 4 lethal damage.
model_solution:
1. Tap Forest, Forest and both Fetid Pools to cast Quarry Hauler ({3}{G}). Leave Weaver of Currents untapped. When Hauler enters, target Kiora, Master of the Depths and put one more loyalty counter on her, taking her from 7 to 8.
2. Activate Kiora's −8. You first get the emblem ("Whenever a creature you control enters, you may have it fight target creature"). Then three 8/8 Octopus tokens are created, so the emblem triggers three times. Choose these targets:
   - Octopus #1 targets Metalwork Colossus A.
   - Octopus #2 targets Metalwork Colossus A.
   - Octopus #3 targets your own Festering Mummy.
3. Resolve the triggers:
   - Octopus #1 fights Colossus A. A takes 8 damage, and the Octopus dies.
   - Octopus #2 fights Colossus A. A now has 16 damage and dies.
   - Octopus #3 fights Festering Mummy. The Mummy dies, and this Octopus survives.
4. The Mummy's death trigger puts a −1/−1 counter on Colossus B. This triggers Hapatra, which creates a 1/1 deathtouch Snake. The Snake entering triggers the emblem: have it fight Colossus B. Damage from a deathtouch source is lethal, so Colossus B dies (the Snake dies too).
5. The opponent now has no creatures. Go to combat and attack with Hapatra (2) and Weaver of Currents (2). Neither is summoning sick, and Weaver is still untapped. That is 4 damage against 4 life, which is lethal. The opponent has no blockers and no possible responses.

Puzzle conventions:
Winning
Unless otherwise stated, you must win the puzzle by inflicting lethal damage to your opponent before the turn ends. This can be as late as during the cleanup step if necessary. Your solution must work for all possible outcomes, such as your opponent’s actions and blocking decisions (see below.)
Phase
Unless otherwise stated, you begin each puzzle at the beginning of your first main phase. You have already drawn a card and gone past upkeep triggers. You have not yet played a land, cast any spells, activated any abilities of permanents on the battlefield, or attacked.
Your Opponent’s Resources / Actions
Unless otherwise stated, your opponent has no cards in hand and no other permanents in play (including no lands – despite the lack of realism there.) This means the only actions you need to consider are activated abilities with no mana cost. Most puzzles with opponent actions will offer more information on this.
Blocking
You cannot assume that your opponent will block a certain way, unless they are somehow forced to. Your solution must satisfy all possible blocking scenarios, even ones that would seem strange in a regular game, and always deal lethal in order to be correct.
Dice
Sometimes you will see six-sided dice placed on cards. These are meant to indicate counters, of whatever type is most reasonable to be there. On most creatures they will be +1/+1 counters, on most artifacts and lands they will be charge counters, and on most Planeswalkers they will be loyalty counters.
If the card specifies a type of counter itself, however (like Icatian Javelineers or Raging Ravine), that will dictate which type it is. 
For -1/-1 counters, we will use a separate graphic to avoid confusion.
Zones
Unless otherwise stated, all zones not displayed are empty. Neither you nor your opponent have cards in graveyards or in exile.
Cards Drawn from Libraries
In any puzzle in which either player might draw cards or otherwise access their library, the puzzle will stipulate some known or assumed information about the library.
Most commonly, this will be a statement that you should assume that the cards remaining in libraries are to be assumed to be irrelevant to the puzzle.
Your Life
Occasionally, your own life total might appear to matter – for cards like Anguished Unmaking, for example. If we require you to consider your own life total in a puzzle, it will be displayed.
If your life total is not shown, you may assume it is irrelevant and effectively infinite.

When you are ready to answer, put your final winning line inside <solution> tags:

<solution>

2. Second step...
</solution>

Your line must be legal under the rules and must win against all possible opponent responses and blocking decisions.

content.thinking:
I'm mapping out the board state: Kiora at 7 loyalty, two Fetid Pools, two Forests, Weaver of Currents, plus Festering Mummy, Hapatra, and Weaver as creatures, against an opponent at 4 life behind two 10/10 blockers. I'm checking whether Kiora's -8 ultimate is reachable, thinking Quarry Hauler might help push the loyalty higher.

The emblem creates three 8/8 Octopus tokens that fight, but since they're summoning sick and only 8/8 against a 10/10, that alone won't get there. I'm exploring using Mockery of Nature's emerge cost with sacrificing Quarry Hauler or Festering Mummy to trigger Hapatra's ability, since a -1/-1 counter would spawn a deathtouch snake that could fight and kill a 10/10 colossus through the emblem's trigger.

Working through the octopus fight sequence: octopus 1 fights colossus A dealing 8 damage while dying to the 10/10, octopus 2 finishes off A, and octopus 3 hits colossus B for 8 damage, leaving it damaged but alive — then Splendid Agony's two -1/-1 counters could shrink B down to 8/8 to finish the job.

Now I'm counting mana: Beast Hauler costs 3G, and its ETB adds a loyalty counter to Kiora before I -8 her, leaving only 2 mana afterward — not enough for Splendid Agony's {2}{B} cost, so I can't do both in the same turn. I'm considering the Hapatra angle instead: since her emblem makes any -1/-1 counter placement spawn a deathtouch snake, Festering Mummy dying could trigger that chain too.

I'm working out whether an octopus's fight trigger can target Festering Mummy itself — fighting my own creature is legal since it just says "target creature." If an octopus fights and kills Mummy, its death trigger puts a -1/-1 counter on another creature, which under the emblem spawns a snake that then fights that same creature, dealing lethal deathtouch damage (though the snake dies too). So I'm trying to sequence the octopuses efficiently: some fight to kill one target while one specifically fights Mummy to chain into the counter-snake-fight combo on another target.

Refining the plan: two octopi kill target A outright, the third kills Mummy and puts a counter on B, then the resulting snake fights and finishes off B. That leaves Hapatra and Weaver as the only attackers for 4 damage total, which is exactly lethal if the opponent's at 4 — I just need to confirm mana works out so Weaver stays untapped (using Forest, another Forest, and two Fetid Pools for the Hauler's cost) and that no blockers survive to stop the attack.

No excess mana needed elsewhere. The emblem is already in play before the octopi enter, so its fight trigger applies to each one as they resolve, with no way for the opponent to interfere given they have no available resources to respond.

Since the fight deals damage as deathtouch damage from the source, the 8/8 kills the 10/10 outright, so the math checks out. I'm ready to write up the final solution.
